Yes, using your credit card for gas every week is definitely killing you in interest — and here's why it's doing you the most harm.

That means the minute the gas company card charges your account, the interest starts to compound. Even if you pay off the balance in full every month, the issuers still charge you a hefty annual points fee just for the convenience of using their card at the pump.  

Also, gas company cards are embedded with chips that log your frequent purchases under your name, which leans into the "building credit" myth. The truth is, those so-called "smart purchases" bloat your credit score with unnecessary debt and trap you into missing out on valuable rewards that come from other card loyalty programs.  

Closer to home, relying on weekly gas card charges creates a mental conditioning — you begin to think of fueling your car not as a cost, but as a routine credit line usage. That psychological shift makes it much easier to charge other less essential items, all while the interest rate climbs higher because you’re using credit more frequently.  

In the long run, paying 18% or more in interest alone on a weekly gas charge could easily cost you more than the gas itself — but it's too late to break the habit before your credit score is permanently compromised. The damage isn't just financial; it's behavioral. You've already given in, and now you're clearing your balance every month instead of actually saving money, which is far more crucial.
